title: Check your understanding: Amending a Commit

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of amending a commit?
options: `git commit --amend` replaces the latest commit with a new commit object, so the commit ID changes. It is convenient for private, unshared history but requires coordination if others already based work on the old commit.
Git automatically backs up every file, including ignored and untracked files, to a remote.
The operation grants every contributor write access to the hosted repository.
questions.answer_key: `git commit --amend` replaces the latest commit with a new commit object, so the commit ID changes. It is convenient for private, unshared history but requires coordination if others already based work on the old commit.
questions.explanation: `git commit --amend` replaces the latest commit with a new commit object, so the commit ID changes. It is convenient for private, unshared history but requires coordination if others already based work on the old commit.

questions.prompt: Which command is the most direct starting point for this lesson’s example?
options: git commit --amend -m "Correct the previous commit message"
questions.answer_key: git commit --amend -m "Correct the previous commit message"
questions.explanation: Use `git commit --amend -m "Correct the previous commit message"` as the first inspection/action in the example, and then verify the result with the companion checks in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest general practice when working with amending a commit?
options: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
Run the most destructive option first; the reflog guarantees every file can always be recovered.
Assume the local command also changed the remote and satisfied all hosting-platform policies.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
questions.explanation: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
